text: A quick hedge: this isn't legal advice, and AI regulation moves fast. The goal is conceptual fluency — knowing the landscape so you can ask the right questions and recognize when a project needs real legal review.

GDPR predates generative AI but applies to any system processing personal data. Data minimization — collect only what's needed. The right to explanation. Purpose limitation — data can't silently be reused for another purpose.

The EU AI Act's core idea is risk-tiering: obligations scale with potential harm, not the technology. Unacceptable risk is banned. High risk gets heavy obligations. Limited risk gets transparency rules. Minimal risk stays largely unregulated.

This isn't a separate checkbox exercise. Bias testing is part of what high-risk obligations ask for. PII handling is data minimization in practice. Model cards are close to what documentation requirements describe.
The same model can face completely different obligations depending on what it's used for. Next up: documentation — model cards, and what they're actually for.
